primary_citation: Cal. Code Civ. Proc. §340.5 (MICRA, Stats. 1975, Ch. 2, 2d Ex. Sess., effective 1976-01-01)
short_title: Medical Malpractice Statute of Limitations — 1 Year Discovery / 3 Year Absolute
one_line_rule: Professional negligence actions against health care providers must be filed within one year of discovering the injury and its negligent cause, and no more than three years from the date of injury, with four enumerated tolling exceptions.

evolution_chain.label: Jolly v. Eli Lilly — 'Reason to Suspect' Standard
evolution_chain.source: Jolly v. Eli Lilly & Co., 44 Cal.3d 1103 (1988)

case_law.cite: Jolly v. Eli Lilly & Co., 44 Cal.3d 1103 (1988)
case_law.key_rule: Discovery trigger = 'reason to suspect' the injury was caused by defendant's wrong; specific knowledge not required; duty to investigate once suspicion arises; ignorance of tortfeasor identity does not toll.

case_law.court: California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District
case_law.key_rule: Physician reassurance can delay 'reason to suspect' trigger; bad outcome alone ≠ suspected negligence; second opinion identifying negligence = classic discovery event; objective reasonable-person standard.

sirva.discovery_question: When did Michael have 'reason to suspect' shoulder injury was caused by negligent injection rather than vaccine reaction?
sirva.likely_discovery_event: SIRVA diagnosis by specialist (date to be established from medical records)
sirva.status: May still be within SOL if SIRVA diagnosis was recent; requires verification of diagnosis date
sirva.tolling_theories: Physician reassurance (Foxborough); fraudulent concealment if Walgreens/Wiseman mischaracterized injury

spine_surgery.status: Requires verification — if surgery was 2016-2017, 3-year outer may have run; fraudulent concealment tolling critical
spine_surgery.hrimnak_escape_value: Intentional tort framing → CCP §338(d) 3-year discovery SOL instead of §340.5; may provide additional time
